chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from some of our companions from Sa'id ibn Yasar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Regarding a man who sold a pregnant slave girl while he was unaware of her pregnancy, and the buyer married her, he said: 'He returns her and returns half of one-tenth of her value.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: There is no contradiction between these narrations, because that which is incumbent upon the one who consummates marriage with the slave girl while she is pregnant, and then wishes to return her, is to return with her half of one-tenth of her price. This is what was contained in the hadith of Ibn Sinan, 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr, Muhammad ibn Rashid, and Sa'id ibn Yasar.

As for the narration of 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr which al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated, stating that it is incumbent upon him one-tenth of her value, it is possible that it was a mistake by the transcriber, that 'half' was dropped and 'one-tenth of the value' remained. For we have cited the narration from him, agreeing with the other narrations, regarding the obligation of half of one-tenth of the value, in what was narrated by 'Ali ibn Ibrahim.

And if this narration were precise, it would be permissible to interpret it as referring to the one who consummates marriage with the slave girl while knowing that she is pregnant; in that case, one-tenth of her value is incumbent upon him as a penalty. However, half of one-tenth is incumbent only if he did not know of her pregnancy, consummated marriage with her, and then learned of the pregnancy.

As for the report of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, and his saying that he returns with her 'something', it is not impossible that by 'something' he meant half of one-tenth of her value, because that is possible for him and for others. And when the amount is clarified in another report, this report should be interpreted according to it.

As for the report narrated by Muhammad ibn Muslim, from his saying 'he returns her and clothes her', it is not impossible that he meant to clothe her with clothing equal in value to half of one-tenth of her price. And there is no contradiction between the narrations on this interpretation, in any case.
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for marrying a pregnant slave girl without prior knowledge of her pregnancy?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi presents a detailed juristic analysis of *'uyub* (defects) in slave girls, specifically addressing the financial compensation for returning a pregnant slave when the buyer was unaware of her condition. The text reconciles apparent contradictions in narrations by distinguishing between ignorance and knowledge of the pregnancy, with the standard penalty being half of one-tenth of her value, while also interpreting vague terms like 'something' or 'clothing' as equivalent to this specific deduction.
